newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI Australia eyes Asian resins investments.
newsitem.headline: ICI Australia eyes Asian resins investments.

text.p: Australian chemicals group ICI Australia Ltd said on Monday it was considering investing up to about A$40 million to make adhesives and resins in Indonesia and China.
The company is looking at building a plant in each country, at a cost of up to A$20 million each, ICI Australia managing director Warren Haynes told Reuters.
He was speaking after officially opening a A$17 million expansion to the company's Melbourne adhesives and resins plant.
"It's something we have been investigating for some time," Haynes told Reuters.
Chinese-made fibreboard is of poor quality, but improving, he added.
ICI Australia is 62.4 percent owned by ICI Plc, which plans to sell its stake in the Australian company by the end of 1997.
"Hopefully, it's not too far off...but we are certainly interested," he added.
ICI Australia's sells adhesives and resins to wood-panel manufacturers who use them to make medium-density fibreboard, a timber-based product used in the building industry.
The company's Australian adhesives and resins business is strongly geared to local and offshore housing markets.
Australian-made fibreboard is exported to New Zealand and to Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.
Indonesia is just beginning to move into medium-density fibreboard manufacturing, Haynes said.
